runtime: Node v24.20.0, read from the production function rather than from the build log
meaning: What the production origin serves after the call to action work. Two sweeps, because they answer two different questions and one of them is cheap enough to run over everything.

allFiveHundredUrls.method: one HTTP request per published URL, no browser, which is what a crawler receives
allFiveHundredUrls.note: 24 of the 500 returned no response on the first pass, run six at a time through this container's egress proxy. Re-run one at a time, 23 answered 200 immediately and the twenty fourth answered 200 on each of three further attempts. So the figure is 500 of 500, and the first pass measured this container's concurrency rather than the origin.

browserSweep.method: headless Chromium, one page per surface, family, language and interactive tool mode. Consent accepted through the banner, then the bottom call to action clicked and the dataLayer read back through sessionStorage, because the navigation destroys the array.

theSixThatDidNotRender.what: six of the sixty five browser sessions ended with a blank document: three on an HTTP 502 and three on a ChunkLoadError for a static asset.
theSixThatDidNotRender.whatItIsNot: a defect in these pages. Every one of the six was re-opened in a single browser session afterwards and rendered perfectly: two call to action pairs, both containers, consent flipping on Accept, internal_cta_click and cta_click pushed, and cta_click observed arriving at GA4 with gcs=G111. The chunks the errors named answered 200 with the same byte count on retest. /en/cost-of-living/japan/, which 502ed twice, answered 200 on twenty consecutive requests afterwards.
theSixThatDidNotRender.whatItProbablyIs: this container's egress under concurrency. A browser opens around forty parallel connections per page and the sweep ran sixty five of them back to back; curl, which opens one, got 200 on all 500 URLs.
theSixThatDidNotRender.whatRulesOutTheOrigin: Vercel logs no runtime error and no error level log for this production deployment over the last day. A 502 generated by Vercel would appear there.
theSixThatDidNotRender.honestLimit: this cannot be proven from inside the container. It is recorded rather than dismissed, and the thing to watch is whether real readers see it: Search Console's crawl stats and the GA4 page_view count against the sitemap would both show it.

analyticsOnAnAtlasPage.consentBeforeAccept: gcs=G100, a cookieless ping, which is the Consent Mode v2 design
analyticsOnAnAtlasPage.stillBlockedAtTheContainer: tool_view, tool_start, tool_complete, internal_cta_click and outbound_click are not in the GA4 event tag's trigger, and nine of the twelve dimensions are not in its parameter table. They reach the dataLayer, which is verified above, and stop there. docs/gtm-changes-needed.md has the exact change.

sitemaps.method: the sitemap index fetched, then every atlas-pages sitemap in it, and the URL set diffed against the two page manifests

theTwoThatWereFixed: /en/cost-of-living/colombia/ now serves h1 Cost of living in Colombia, verified on the origin
/de/feiertage/niederlande/ keeps its correct heading and no longer claims a keyword that belongs to the Lower Saxony page
